name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans roughly 20 points Republican, among the most GOP-favorable seats in the country
Incumbent Riley Moore holds a roughly five-to-one fundraising advantage over Ace Parsi
Prediction markets price Moore's win probability near 97 percent
A Democratic-tilted national House environment is the only force narrowing the margin
model.rationale: The district's twenty-point Republican lean, Moore's incumbency and five-to-one money edge, and market pricing near 97 percent for the GOP all point the same direction; a favorable national environment for Democrats may trim the margin a few points but cannot plausibly close a gap this wide.
model.watch: A strong Democratic wave paired with an unexpected Moore misstep could tighten the race, though Parsi would need a major influx of outside money to make it genuinely competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's second district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly twenty points toward the GOP. Riley Moore, the Republican incumbent, is running for re-election and holds a commanding financial edge, having raised about $1.3 million to Democrat Ace Parsi's roughly $250,000, and entering the fall with more than $750,000 on hand. Parsi, a first-time challenger, has shown modest fundraising and drawn little outside support.

Prediction markets give Moore about a 97 percent chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The main force working against Moore is a national environment that has favored Democrats in House races this cycle, which could trim his margin by several points. Even so, the district's fundamentals make an upset highly unlikely, and the seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands.
